scenes.title: Start at a notched corner
scenes.narration: Take a board with two rows and four columns. Lift the first and last squares of the top row. Each domino covers two cells sharing an edge. Which way can a domino go from the bottom left corner?

scenes.title: Fit the three forced pieces
scenes.narration: There is no square above the bottom left corner. Its domino must point right. At the bottom right corner the domino must point left. Only the two middle squares in the top row remain. One last horizontal domino fills them. Every placement was forced.

scenes.title: Work around a glued domino
scenes.narration: A new board has two rows and five columns. One upright domino is glued into the second column. It must stay there. How many ways can you fill the rest? Look at the parts on either side of the fixed piece.

scenes.title: Count the three remaining patterns
scenes.narration: The single column on the left needs one upright domino. The three columns on the right have three patterns. Use three upright dominoes, or put a horizontal pair before one upright domino, or put the pair after it. These are the only patterns because a horizontal domino forces its partner.

scenes.title: Require a crossing at the seam
scenes.narration: A longer board has two rows and six columns. Draw a seam between columns three and four. Count the tilings in which at least one domino crosses the seam. Could exactly one domino cross?

scenes.title: Prove why a second crossing is forced
scenes.narration: Suppose only the top domino crosses. It covers one cell of the six on the left. Five cells would still need covering on that side. Dominoes cover cells in pairs, so five is impossible. The lower domino must cross as well. Two square rooms are left, one on each side.

scenes.title: Multiply the choices in the two rooms
scenes.narration: In either two by two room, use two upright dominoes or two horizontal dominoes. Either choice on the left can go with either choice on the right. Two times two gives four tilings. The fixed crossing pair separates the rooms, so none of the four is counted twice.

scenes.title: Keep upright dominoes apart
scenes.narration: Try a strip with two rows and seven columns. Use exactly three upright dominoes, with no two in neighbouring columns. Four columns remain for two horizontal pairs. Lay down those two pairs first. There are three gaps: before, between and after. Each gap can hold at most one upright domino. All three gaps must be filled. There is exactly one tiling.
